failures: src/sprout/eval/check_run.py, _uses(): `recs[name[:-5]] = ((0, index, ...), ...)` keeps the LAST commit that added a file stem, so deleting a first test-split record and re-adding it (or `git mv` away and back) in a later commit makes it look newer than the second use. The second use then ranks first and passes both `check_run <E#>` and `claims check` with no override_note, so a second look at the test set can yield a published number. Reproduce: tmp-T2.3/t17.py (E9 record, then E2 record on lab_test, `git rm` and re-add the first). The doc rule says the earlier use is the one git added first. Fix: keep the first add per stem (`setdefault`) and add a test for delete and re-add and for mv back.
tests/test_records.py has no case for a record deleted and re-added, or moved and returned, in later commits. The test-once git-order tests pass without covering the flip.
notes: Not failures, but could put a wrong number on record: (1) A test-split record committed outside results/runs (for example results/hold/) is never counted, so a later record passes as the first use. (2) A shared_classes view written in a separate run after results were committed has a different git_commit and is treated as a second use, so it needs an override_note or must be written in the same run as the full record. (3) Same-commit ordering (squash, or two records in one commit) falls back to path order, so records from different experiments can swap order; one of them still fails. (4) A git-less directory was not tested on its own because the temp repos sit inside the main repo. (5) shared_classes on rag_test is rejected as an unknown subset, which is reasonable. (6) results/claims.json is empty, so claims check passes trivially on the real repo. Known limits (git_commit forgery to an older ancestor, seeds, accepted flags, never-committed backdating) were not failed. Nothing was written to the real results/runs/ and the worktree is clean.
